summary: The remaining mismatch is fatal-blast wording after a pyrolisk egg burns the hero’s cloak. C sets iflags.last_msg to CAUGHT_IN_EXPLOSION after the caught message, but the intervening cloak-smouldering message clears it in pline.c:vpline; explode() then prints “The fireball is fatal.” Port this last_msg flow through js/tty_message.js and branch in js/explode.js instead of always printing “It is fatal.”

source.branch: When a non-polymorphed hero takes lethal fire damage from a visible explosion while verbose messages are enabled, explode() emits the caught-in-explosion message and marks iflags.last_msg. If a later pline message (here, the cloak-smouldering item damage message) clears that marker before the fatal-message branch, C uses pline_The("%s is fatal.", str); otherwise it uses "It is fatal.".
callers: eat.c:fprefx (2099-2109) consumes an EGG laid by PM_PYROLISK and calls explode(u.ux, u.uy, -11, d(3, 6), 0, EXPL_FIERY); js/eat.js:fprefx (3179-3185) is the corresponding production caller.
explode.c:explode (594-603, 668-675) marks the caught-in-explosion message and later selects fatal wording; js/explode.js:explode (655-692) is the corresponding runtime implementation.
dependencies: pline.c:vpline (280-281) resets iflags.last_msg to PLNMSG_UNKNOWN after a displayed message. Implement the same emitted-message reset in js/tty_message.js so the intervening cloak message cancels the explosion marker before js/explode.js selects fatal wording.

evidence: The saved queue entry from challenges/evaluations/20261006225046-v24.json at 84d84e111155ac834c43327b7c696055df294349 has 29/30 matching screens and cursors and 2540/2540 matching RNG calls. Its first mismatch is step 27 after Space: the C/JS first cells are T/I and the cursor columns are 30/20. The one-session diagnostic replay reproduces this signature; it reports replay revision 3470fce7b2ee7ab949c421ea2abd70fac3854b4e, whose js/eat.js, js/explode.js, and js/tty_message.js files are unchanged at the examined 84d84e1 commit.
C eat.c:fprefx (2102-2109) consumes the pyrolisk egg and calls explode() with type -11 and EXPL_FIERY. The matching JS eat.js:fprefx branch reaches js/explode.js:explode with the same fireball route.

C explode.c:explode sets iflags.last_msg to PLNMSG_CAUGHT_IN_EXPLOSION after its caught message (602-603). It applies fire damage and item effects before checking the marker at 668-672. The recorded step 26 includes “Your cloak smoulders!”, so pline.c:vpline has cleared the marker by the fatal wording; C therefore emits “The fireball is fatal.”

JS explode.js:explode (655-692) neither sets the caught-in-explosion marker nor chooses between the source branches; it always sends “It is fatal.” The JS TTY pipeline in tty_message.js (453-582) does not apply pline.c:vpline’s last_msg reset after an emitted message. Fix the narrow state/message contract in those two existing implementations.
